key_provisions_or_claims: Participants (older people, informal and formal carers) favoured compromise, persuasion and negotiation to resolve value conflicts over robot use.
Autonomy generally has priority over other values, except in certain safety cases.
Robot roles, role-norms and hypothetical user-provider agreements help resolve tensions.
Participants disapproved of robots asserting themselves or being coercive in enablement.
Values should be built into robot design and into the process of introducing robots into homes.
annotation.summary_en: Qualitative study of 21 focus groups (123 participants in France, Netherlands, UK) with older people and carers on ethical values—autonomy, safety, enablement, independence, privacy, social connectedness—and their tensions in social care robots (ACCOMPANY project). Autonomy usually takes priority except sometimes safety; the paper discusses operationalising the values in robot design.
annotation.title_clean: Ethical values and social care robots for older people: an international qualitative study
annotation.title_en: Ethical values and social care robots for older people: an international qualitative study
